name: HyperStrong (Beijing HyperStrong Technology)
headquarters: Haidian District, Beijing, China (US offices: Houston, Chicago, San Francisco)
employees: Not disclosed (R&D staff 200+, 70% with advanced degrees — company-claimed)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: HyperStrong is China's dominant asset-light BESS integrator — 60+ GWh deployed across 400+ projects, #1 domestically by cumulative installed capacity, top-3-to-top-5 globally depending on whose methodology you trust — riding a 229% first-day IPO pop (STAR Market, January 2025) and a ~500% 2025 stock run driven substantially by the AI-data-center energy narrative. It buys its cells (a ≥200 GWh ten-year CATL pact plus 50 GWh from EVE and the world's largest sodium-ion order) and sells integration, EPC and AI-driven operations. BACKGROUND: Founded 2011 by Dr. Zhang Jianhui — Tsinghua, UC Berkeley PhD, National Semiconductor, then CTO of Siemens China's smart-grid unit. FY2025: revenue RMB 11.61B (+40%), net profit RMB 951M (+47%); storage is 99.9% of revenue. Overseas is only ~8% of revenue but growing 77% and carrying the margin: ~10 GWh of 2026 overseas orders are locked (Europe 40%, Americas 35% — the Americas slice described as data-center storage projects with multiple asset operators). Flagship Western reference: the 1.6 GWh LEAG GigaBattery Boxberg EPC in Germany (HyperBlock III, completion 2026). US traction is real but small — Houston HQ, a Luminous Energy MoU, and a company-claimed 420+ MWh delivered — and the FEOC regime caps it: a Chinese integrator wrapping Chinese cells is close to all-prohibited-content for ITC purposes.
ecosystemRole: We assess HyperStrong as the purest test of whether integration skill alone can cross the Pacific: it owns no cells, no PCS fab of consequence, and no US manufacturing — its assets are systems engineering, an AI operations stack, and the deepest domestic project base in China. That model produced domestic dominance and a genuine European beachhead, but under the FEOC material-assistance rules a HyperStrong system is essentially all-prohibited-content, leaving its US lane to safe-harbored projects and tax-credit-indifferent buyers. For the Hithium-centric view of this ecosystem the relationship is double-edged: HyperStrong is simultaneously a major cell customer of CATL/EVE (and via CRRC's supply web adjacent to Hithium's), a direct competitor in containerized systems, and the proof that the 2026-28 Chinese order books (300 GWh cumulative target) are being written at home and in Europe/MEA — not in the US.

productsAndServices.name: HyperBlock M (12.8 MWh modular flagship, 2025-26)
productsAndServices.description: Modular 10-ft 'MagicBlock' architecture — 1/2/4/8-block configurations side-by-side or back-to-back, 24-tonne modules. AC version integrates self-developed 400 kW SiC PCS units (max efficiency 99.3%) at 690 Vac; DC versions carry 12.8 MWh on 601 Ah LFP or 12.523 MWh on 588 Ah. RTE ≥93% at 4-hour duration; >10,000 cycles to 70% SOH; dual-channel liquid cooling (-20% cooling energy); grid-forming, black start, islanding. Seven TÜV Rheinland certifications (April 2026) plus UL 9540/9540A/1973/1741, IEEE 1547, NFPA 855/68/69. Semi-automated one-hour battery-module swap; HyperGenie AI O&M assistant. Mass delivery began February 2026.
productsAndServices.positioning: The largest modular block in the field — twice the energy of the 5-6 MWh generation — aimed at utility-scale everywhere including North America.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct supply, full EPC, and partner-led development (LEAG, Repono, GOLDBECK, Redelfi, Luminous)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Global rollout following the April 2026 TÜV certifications

productsAndServices.name: HyperBlock III (5 MWh workhorse)
productsAndServices.description: 5,016 kWh per 20-ft container on 314 Ah LFP (12P416S), 2,500 kW, liquid-cooled. Passed a five-unit back-to-back large-scale fire test at 100% SOC with no suppression (January 2026) under CSA/ANSI C800:2025 and the latest UL 9540A draft — 16-hour burn, 1,400°C peak, no propagation, adjacent-unit peak cell temperature 56°C.
productsAndServices.positioning: The delivery vehicle for the European flagship (LEAG 1.6 GWh) and the US-permitting proof point.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Superseded at the flagship tier by HyperBlock M; a 7 MWh-class 587 Ah system is already field-deployed in China (Baotou 2.4 GWh)

productsAndServices.name: HyperCube C&I line (835.9 kWh Max / 261 kWh Plus)
productsAndServices.description: HyperCube C&I II Max: 835.9 kWh on 314 Ah cells with transformer-free 400/690/800 Vac architecture, SiC, liquid cooling, RTE 92%, PCS efficiency to 99.3% — marketed as 'ideal for AI data centers and future high-load applications.' The 261 kWh Plus cabinet runs the 'Darwin' self-evolving thermal algorithm and parallels to 20 units.
productsAndServices.positioning: The AIDC-facing edge of the portfolio — no dedicated data-center product line exists; these cabinets carry that positioning.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Commercial parks, EV charging, data centers
productsAndServices.roadmap: 'Energy Storage + X' strategy (June 2025) names data centers, oilfields, mining and telecom as target verticals

productsAndServices.name: Cell supply agreements (the asset-light hedge)
productsAndServices.description: CATL: ten-year agreement (2026-2035) with ≥200 GWh of procurement over 2026-2028 (~RMB 20B scale), plus a 60 GWh three-year sodium-ion order (April 2026 — claimed world's largest, applications including data-center storage). EVE Power: 50 GWh over 2025-2027. Historical mix: CATL supplied 81% of cells in 2022, 63% in 2023; H1 2024 CATL 21% vs EVE 35% — then re-concentration via the CATL pact.
productsAndServices.positioning: Supply security bought with dependence — locked volume through the 2025-26 cell tightening at undisclosed pricing, from suppliers who are also downstream competitors.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Sodium-ion commercialization for long-duration and remote-region storage 2026-2029

productsAndServices.name: AI operations stack (HyperStrong AI Platform, HyperGenie)
productsAndServices.description: AI/big-data/digital-twin platform spanning production management, station performance optimization and fault diagnosis; HyperGenie O&M assistant trained on 200+ global cases and 50+ expert models; claimed 7-day-advance thermal-runaway early warning.
productsAndServices.positioning: The software layer is the differentiation claim for an integrator that owns no cell chemistry — and the CEO's stated pivot from price competition to lifecycle value.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with systems and O&M contracts
productsAndServices.roadmap: Extends across the 300 GWh 2026-28 delivery target

recentDevelopments.headline: H1 2026 forecast: revenue RMB 5.6-6.9B (+24-53%), net profit RMB 620-700M (+96-122%) — profit growing roughly twice as fast as revenue on overseas mix
recentDevelopments.read: The margin story is overseas: ~8% of revenue carrying an outsized share of profit growth, which is exactly why the 10 GWh overseas order book matters more than its size suggests.

recentDevelopments.headline: ~10 GWh of 2026 overseas orders locked: Europe 40%, Americas 35%, SEA+other 25% — the North America component described as data-center energy storage projects with multiple asset operators
recentDevelopments.read: The most concrete AIDC signal in the file — unnamed operators, unbroken US/LatAm split, but a stated data-center order book in the Americas from a supplier the FEOC regime nominally locks out of ITC projects. Tax-credit-indifferent data-center configurations are the plausible lane.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess HyperStrong's ranking story as methodology-dependent and China-weighted: top-3 (S&P, 2024 installs) and #5 (InfoLink shipments, 2024 and 1H25) coexist with complete absence from Wood Mackenzie's and Benchmark's 2025 global top-10s. Basis: the four rankings themselves. The defensible statement is domestic #1 cumulative, top-5 by shipments through mid-2025, with ~86% of volume still Chinese.

(High confidence) We assess the integrator-without-cells model as deliberately hedged rather than fixed: the ≥200 GWh CATL pact and 50 GWh EVE agreement lock supply through the 2025-26 tightening, but pricing terms are undisclosed and both suppliers sell competing systems. Basis: disclosed supplier-mix history (CATL 81% of cells in 2022 → 21% in H1 2024 → re-concentration via the pact).

(Moderate confidence) We assess the US position as structurally capped but deliberately kept alive: Houston/Chicago/San Francisco offices, the Luminous MoU, NA-registered-FPE fire testing and the full UL certification stack are real investments, while FEOC makes a Chinese integrator wrapping Chinese cells close to all-prohibited-content for ITC purposes. The company's own 2026 Americas order framing — data-center storage with multiple asset operators — points at the tax-credit-indifferent lane as the intended US path. The 420+ MWh US delivery claim remains unverified by any third party.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the AIDC narrative as ahead of the AIDC book: the ~500% 2025 stock run leaned on AI-energy demand, but disclosed data-center wins are pilots and unnamed operators; no hyperscaler or colocation customer is named anywhere. The capability set (HyperBlock M grid-forming, transformer-free 800 Vac C&I cabinets, sodium-ion for data-center storage) is genuinely AIDC-relevant — the revenue is not yet visible.

(Moderate confidence) We assess execution concentration as the near-term risk that matters: the LEAG 1.6 GWh EPC is the largest Western reference and completes in 2026; a slip there damages the European franchise that carries the margin story. Domestically, CRRC's SOE machine has already displaced HyperStrong from #1 on new installs, and S&P's 'thin to zero margin' read on Chinese integration underlines why overseas execution is existential.

relationships.note: Ten-year pact (2026-2035): ≥200 GWh over 2026-28 (~RMB 20B) plus the claimed world's largest sodium-ion order — supply security at the cost of structural dependence.
relationships.context:
The November 2025 strategic pact locks ≥200 GWh of cells and systems over 2026-2028 (Morgan Stanley sized it at roughly half of CATL's 2025 ESS volume annually), plus joint investment funds; April 2026 added a 60 GWh three-year sodium-ion agreement with applications including data-center storage.

The history shows deliberate hedging: CATL supplied 81% of HyperStrong's cells in 2022, down to 21% in H1 2024 (EVE 35%), then re-concentration via the pact. Both suppliers also sell competing systems downstream — the integrator-without-cells model's structural tension.

relationships.note: 50 GWh cell supply agreement — the counterweight to CATL dependence.
relationships.context: EVE agreed a 50 GWh battery cell supply deal with HyperStrong (February 2025), the second leg of the asset-light hedge. In H1 2024 EVE was briefly HyperStrong's largest cell source (35% vs CATL's 21%) before the CATL pact re-concentrated the mix.

relationships.note: Direct containerized-systems rival writing the 2026-28 Chinese order book Hithium also chases.
relationships.context: HyperStrong is simultaneously a major cell customer of CATL/EVE and a direct competitor to Hithium in containerized systems — and its 300 GWh cumulative order-book target is proof the 2026-28 Chinese storage boom is being written at home and in Europe/MEA, not in the US.
